newsitem.title: DUBAI: HORSE RACING-FAVOURITE SIPHON DRAWS WIDE CUP START.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-FAVOURITE SIPHON DRAWS WIDE CUP START.

text.p: Siphon, the California-trained, Brazilian-bred favourite to win Saturday's $4 million Dubai World Cup, drew 10th out from the rail on Tuesday in a 13-horse field.
Trainer Richard Mandella, whose other horse in Dubai -- second favourite Sandpit -- drew 12, was philosophical about his chances in the world's richest horse race.
"Well, it's better to come with two bullets than one," said Mandella after the post position draw for the 2,000 metres (mile and a quarter) race on a desert sand track on Saturday night.

British bookmakers on Tuesday made Siphon, winner of the Santa Anita Handicap earlier this month and the 1996 Hollywood Gold Cup, the 5-2 favourite. Sandpit, also Brazilian-owned and placed second at Santa Anita, was close behind at 7-2.
Gambling is banned in the United Arab Emirates but bookies Ladbrokes have an odds-maker in Dubai.
The 13-horse field, all Group One winners, between them have been first past the post 96 times and have collectively won $22 million, said race committee chairman Michael Osborne.
Their average rating of 122 had never before been achieved in a race with 13 runners, he said.
"This is the highest collective calibre ever staged," Osborne said at the post position draw which was also attended by Britain's Prince Edward.
Post position went to Even Top, German-born Benny Schmidt-Bodner's four-year-old colt trained in England by Mark Tompkins.
Singspiel, the Japan Cup winner owned by World Cup host Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, the world's most successful owner-breeder, will start from the second gate.

Next is the William Perry-trained Formal Gold of the United States and then Europe's champion, French horse Helissio, the Elie Lellouche-trained winner of the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe who was rated the world's best three-year-old last year.
Betting: Siphon 5-2, Sandpit 7-2, Helissio 9-2, Formal Gold, Singspiel 6-1, Kammtarra 8-1, Flemensfirth 10-1, Key of Luck 20-1, Even Top, Juggler 25-1, Bijou D'Inde, Hokuto Vega, Luso 33-1.
